To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time–dependent rate equations for a quasi-two–level system with wavelength dependent emission and absorption cross–sections are a reliable tool to simulate the characteristic laser behaviour of optically pumped Er–doped waveguide lasers, and that the algorithmic replacement procedure, which was developed to solve the rate equations, is a useful tool to treat large boundary value problems of ordinary differential equations in the field of nonlinear optics.

the relaxation oscillations of Er–doped waveguide lasers are caused by a combination of two different mechanisms: the population relaxation in the active medium, and the dynamical response of the resonator.
the relaxation oscillations of an erbium–doped waveguide laser can be simulated by a time–dependent rate equation model with a numerically reliable algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulation of the time–dependent behavior of optically pumped erbium–doped waveguide lasers.
the analysis and numerical simulation of the dynamic behaviour of optically pumped erbium doped planar waveguide laser systems.
a theoretical investigation of the dynamics of optically pumped wave-guide lasers.
